title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: The Muscat talks ended on Tuesday with no deal on Hormuz, and tanker strikes went on off Oman. Air is the other pressure point: Dubai-to-Europe air rates are up 83% on last year, and Etihad has cancelled Riyadh and Dammam cargo flights to 30 November.

stories.headline: Muscat talks end with no Hormuz deal
body: Iran's Abbas Araghchi and Oman's Badr Albusaidi met in Muscat on Tuesday. Oman said the talks focused on maritime security and keeping shipping moving. There was no joint statement and no timeline.
Albusaidi called the talks "constructive". But unlike Oman's 5 November readout, Tuesday's statements did not mention reopening the strait. The US naval blockade of Iran stays in place.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: the one near-term route to lower surcharges did not deliver. Plan on Hormuz staying restricted into December.

stories.headline: More tanker strikes off Khasab; one seafarer missing
body: The LPG carrier Tara Gas was hit north of Khasab, Oman. One seafarer is missing and two are injured, and India says they are Indian nationals. UKMTO also reported a tanker disabled with an engine-room fire off Oman overnight.

Iran's navy says a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels and an LNG carrier hit mines. No maritime authority has confirmed the mine claims. IMF PortWatch logged just 2 transits on 15 November.
stories.soWhat: Crew casualties push insurers harder. Expect war-risk cover and Gulf-bound sea rates to stay high this week.

stories.headline: Iran says US struck Qeshm Island after drones hit at Bahrain
body: Iranian media say US forces hit several sites on Qeshm Island, in the strait, on Tuesday. This came hours after the IRGC said it targeted a US radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain. CENTCOM said the drones were intercepted with no damage.
No US official has confirmed the Qeshm strikes. Iran says there was no damage to homes, shops or infrastructure.
stories.soWhat: Fighting is now on both sides of the Gulf. Keep Bahrain and Hormuz-area service notes current for customers.

stories.headline: flydubai back in Dammam; Etihad cancels Riyadh and Dammam cargo to 30 Nov
body: flydubai has resumed Dammam on a reduced schedule. Riyadh and Abha stay suspended until 27 November, and the airline expects more disruption.
Etihad has cancelled all passenger and cargo flights from Abu Dhabi to Riyadh and Dammam through Monday 30 November. Its other Saudi flights run as scheduled.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: the flydubai ban was extended, not lifted. UAE-to-Riyadh air capacity stays thin for two more weeks, so road is the product.

stories.headline: Dubai air rates to Europe up 83% on last year
body: WorldACD data for 2–8 November show global air cargo rates up 2% on the week to $3.45 per kg, and 31% on last year. Middle East and South Asia rates are up 63% year on year, the most of any region.
From Dubai, rates to Europe are up 83% and to the US more than 80%. Saudi chargeable weight is down as much as 33% against week 40 after Houthi missile attacks.
stories.soWhat: Air buy rates out of Dubai are far above last year. Check our air sell rates and fuel and war surcharges keep pace.

competitors.name: Etihad Cargo
competitors.headline: Riyadh and Dammam cargo flights off until 30 November
body: Etihad has cancelled all cargo and passenger flights from Abu Dhabi to Riyadh and Dammam through 30 November. Other Abu Dhabi to Saudi flights operate as scheduled.
competitors.soWhat: Shippers lose a direct belly and cargo option into Saudi's two biggest business cities. Our UAE-Saudi road service can pick up that freight.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: New Milan–New York freighter from 5 December
body: Emirates SkyCargo will fly a weekly Boeing 777-F from Milan to New York JFK from 5 December, with around 100 tonnes per flight. It also runs a weekly Milan–Dubai DWC freighter.
Eight new freighters joined this year, and its freighter network grew from over 40 destinations in March to over 60 in July.
competitors.soWhat: Emirates is putting freighter capacity on lanes outside the Gulf. Dubai-origin capacity for our air products may stay tight and dear.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Record Q3 revenue, but thinner margin
body: Q3 revenue was a record Dh1.98 billion, up 24%, and net profit rose to Dh48 million. Gross margin narrowed to 21% from 23.2%. No newer figure has been published.
competitors.soWhat: With Dubai air rates up 83%, protecting margin on air and forwarding matters more than volume.

opportunities.title: UAE–Saudi road freight
opportunities.text: flydubai is off Riyadh to 27 November and Etihad off Riyadh and Dammam to 30 November. Sell road as the reliable option.

opportunities.title: Dammam air is back, partly
opportunities.text: flydubai's reduced Dammam schedule gives some belly space. Offer a premium Dammam air option while it is scarce.

opportunities.title: Price air to the market
opportunities.text: Dubai-to-Europe and Dubai-to-US rates are up 80% or more on last year. There is room to lift air yields where we lag the market.

opportunities.title: East-coast routing
opportunities.text: With no Hormuz deal, Khor Fakkan and Fujairah routing stays the main bypass. Keep pushing it to key importers.

watchouts.title: No deal in Muscat
watchouts.text: Hormuz restrictions look set to run into December. Sea surcharges will not ease soon.

watchouts.title: Crew casualties
watchouts.text: A missing seafarer on Tara Gas raises the stakes for insurers and owners. Expect fewer sailings and higher cover costs.

watchouts.title: Saudi air volumes falling
watchouts.text: Saudi chargeable weight is down up to 33% against week 40. Inbound Saudi air revenue will be weak.

watchouts.title: Margin squeeze on air
watchouts.text: Buy rates out of Dubai are up sharply. Contract customers on fixed rates can erode our margin.

watchouts.title: Bahrain exposure
watchouts.text: Iran says it has targeted Bahrain three times in a week. Have contingency plans for Bahrain shipments.

moves.title: Roll the 'no deal' surcharge setting
moves.text: Muscat gave no Hormuz deal. Keep current war-risk pass-through on sea quotes and review it again next week.

moves.title: Audit air sell rates against WorldACD
moves.text: Compare our Dubai-to-Europe and Dubai-to-US air sell rates with the 80%+ market rise and fix lanes that lag.

moves.title: Push UAE–Saudi road to Riyadh shippers
moves.text: Tell customers flydubai is off Riyadh to 27 November and Etihad to 30 November, and offer road capacity now.

moves.title: Offer limited Dammam air
moves.text: Check flydubai's reduced Dammam schedule for belly space and price it as a premium option.

moves.title: Review fixed-rate air contracts
moves.text: Flag key accounts on fixed air rates set before the rise and open surcharge talks.

moves.title: Update Bahrain and Oman service notes
moves.text: After the Bahrain drone attacks and Khasab tanker strikes, refresh customer advisories for these lanes.
